meta.title: "Do it or it'll be a disaster": real danger or is your child just being wound up? | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to tell a real warning from inflated fear: are there facts, is there logic, or is it just words? Game-based critical thinking course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: Does your child react to every "scary" the same way?
hero.subheadline: "Go or you'll miss your chance." "Do it or it'll be a disaster." "Buy it or you'll regret it." It sounds serious — and your child reacts automatically, because they have no way to tell real danger from hype.

media.alt: A child unable to tell real danger from inflated fear

pain.title: Not every fear is true
pain.body:
There are real warnings: where there's a clear "cause → effect" link and the danger genuinely exists. And there are exaggerations, where the fear is simply inflated to make someone act. The trouble is, both sound equally convincing — "it'll be bad" is said with the same tone either way.

This isn't being scared of everything or cowardice. The child simply has no tool to check: is there fact behind this fear, or only words? So they take any "scary" as a signal to act, without telling a warning apart from pressure.

The result — the child gives in even where nothing is actually at stake. They agree, rush, give up their own position — because "what if it's true", even though a loud phrase often has no real consequence behind it at all.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
